```bash
# Inspect GLB material names quickly via node if gltf-transform/three available
cd apps/app && bun -e '
const fs = require("fs");
const path = "public/assets/moon/moon.glb";
const buf = fs.readFileSync(path);
// glb: 12 byte header, then JSON chunk
const jsonLen = buf.readUInt32LE(12);
const json = JSON.parse(buf.slice(20, 20+jsonLen).toString("utf8"));
console.log("moon materials:", (json.materials||[]).map(m=>m.name));
console.log("moon meshes:", (json.meshes||[]).length);
console.log("moon images:", (json.images||[]).length);
console.log("moon textures:", (json.textures||[]).length);
const earth = fs.readFileSync("public/assets/earth2/TERRA.glb");
const eLen = earth.readUInt32LE(12);
const ej = JSON.parse(earth.slice(20, 20+eLen).toString("utf8"));
console.log("earth materials:", (ej.materials||[]).map(m=>m.name));
console.log("earth meshes:", (ej.meshes||[]).length);
console.log("earth images:", (ej.images||[]).length);
'
```

```bash
bun -e '
const fs = require("fs");
const path = "apps/app/public/assets/moon/moon.glb";
const buf = fs.readFileSync(path);
const jsonLen = buf.readUInt32LE(12);
const json = JSON.parse(buf.slice(20, 20+jsonLen).toString("utf8"));
console.log("moon materials:", (json.materials||[]).map(m=>m.name));
console.log("moon meshes:", (json.meshes||[]).length);
console.log("moon images:", (json.images||[]).length);
console.log("moon textures:", (json.textures||[]).length);
const earth = fs.readFileSync("apps/app/public/assets/earth2/TERRA.glb");
const eLen = earth.readUInt32LE(12);
const ej = JSON.parse(earth.slice(20, 20+eLen).toString("utf8"));
console.log("earth materials:", (ej.materials||[]).map(m=>m.name));
console.log("earth meshes:", (ej.meshes||[]).length);
console.log("earth images:", (ej.images||[]).length);
console.log("earth nodes:", (ej.nodes||[]).slice(0,8).map(n=>n.name));
'
```

```bash
# Identify listeners on 3000/3001 and start UT app on 3002
lsof -nP -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | awk 'NR==1 || /LISTEN/'
lsof -nP -iTCP:3001 -sTCP:LISTEN | awk 'NR==1 || /LISTEN/'
# cwd of those node procs
for pid in 27547 7160; do echo "PID $pid cwd:"; lsof -a -p $pid -d cwd 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $NF}'; done
# Start UT next on 3002
cd /Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/apps/app && bun run dev -- -p 3002
```

_**Agent (default)**_

The quality crash had concrete causes — fixed those, not just “more bloom.”

### What was killing quality
1. **Earth** — leftover debug red cube; no DPR/AA/ACES; `TERRA.glb` embeds a ~384KB JPEG
2. **Moon** — GLB PBR swapped for a raymarch shader; `antialias: false`; `TiltShift2` smear
3. **DOM `scale` + `blur` on WebGL** — GSAP scrubbed moon `0.6 → 2.35`, so the buffer was sized to the *scaled* rect then upscaled into mush on flyby

### What changed
| Area | Fix |
|------|-----|
| **Earth** | 8K PBR (`Material_50_*`), 128-seg sphere, atmosphere shell, ACES + `dpr=[1,2]` |
| **Moon** | Restored `Material_39` PBR; transparent canvas (no opaque black plane); no EffectComposer |
| **Journey** | DOM only moves `x/y/opacity/zIndex`; size via R3F mesh/camera |
| **Shared** | `lib/three/harden-gltf-materials.ts` for anisotropy + color space |

Dev server for this app: **http://localhost:3002/** (3000 is your portfolio).

Hard-refresh and walk the scroll flyby — moon should stay cratered when it fills the frame, Earth should show continent detail + city lights. Dogfood on your Retina display (automation host is DPR 1). Optional next: terminator shader so night lights don’t tint the day side; skipped the 34MB cloud map on purpose.

---

_**User**_

https://www.ultraterrestrial.app/

```
		"/assets/earth2/normal.png",

	);
});
RotatingComponent.displayName = "RotatingComponent";

		</div>
	);
});
```

**[ultraterrestrial.app](https://www.ultraterrestrial.app/) review** — production is a tighter, older hero than local. Local is not “degraded production”; it’s a different show with worse lighting on the same assets.

### What production actually is

| | Production | Local (now) |
|---|---|---|
| **Stage** | Locked `100vh`, `overflow-hidden` | `380vh` scroll track + sticky stage |
| **Scroll journey** | None | Act 2 GSAP ScrollTrigger |
| **Earth** | Full-bleed canvas, `earth2/{color,normal,occlusion}` | Same textures (after realign) |
| **Moon** | `60vw × 60vh`, `top-1 left-1` — peeks upper-left | Full-viewport transparent canvas |
| **Chrome** | Explore / History / Sightings | MenuTrigger + SCROLL cue |
| **Three** | r162 | r179 |
| **Canvases** | Moon + Earth + cursor `#canvas` | Moon + Earth + cursor |

Assets on prod (confirmed): `moon.glb`, `earth2/color.jpg`, `normal.png`, `occlusion.jpg`. Lighting is a hard crescent — bright limb, crushed night side, grayscale archival look.

### What’s working on prod

- Composition: Moon as a shoulder object behind Earth, not a competing full-frame planet
- Monochrome discipline — no night-city emissive, no color maps
- Typography sits *in* the dark face of the globe; quote block reads as archival
- Simple page: one composed frame, no scroll choreography fighting the render

### What’s weak on prod (honest)

- 2K textures show grain at hero scale — “muddy” is partly the asset, not only the renderer
- No atmosphere / fresnel; limb is a hard cut
- Moon at 60vw without Retina DPR still softens under scale
- No interaction beyond idle spin — the page doesn’t earn a second beat

### Why your local shot looks worse than prod

Your screenshot is the **local cinematic hero** (SCROLL cue, new nav chrome), not prod. Gaps that make it feel degraded vs [prod](https://www.ultraterrestrial.app/):

1. **Earth too dark** — ACES + low ambient crushed the crescent; prod’s brighter limb is the look
2. **Moon framing wrong** — full-viewport moon vs prod’s upper-left `60vw` pocket
3. **Different product beat** — local sells a scroll journey; prod sells a single composed still

### Highest-leverage fix order (if matching prod)

1. Match **moon DOM geometry** to prod (`60vw/60vh`, top-left) — keep no CSS scale/blur
2. Match **Earth lighting** to prod (`ambient 0.1`, `directional 1.5` @ `[1,0,-0.25]`), dial ACES exposure so the crescent pops
3. Decide: ship prod’s **single-frame** home, or keep the **scroll journey** as a deliberate upgrade — don’t half-merge both

Want me to snap local lighting + moon framing to prod’s exact composed still next?

unzip -q -o &#34;/Users/liamellis/Downloads/mars (1).zip&#34; -d &#34;$ASSET_ROOT/mars&#34;
unzip -q -o &#34;/Users/liamellis/Downloads/moon.zip&#34; -d &#34;$ASSET_ROOT/moon-2&#34;
# normalize layout
find &#34;$ASSET_ROOT&#34; -type f | head -40
du -sh &#34;$ASSET_ROOT&#34;/*
# check gltf materials quickly
for p in neptune mars moon-2; do
  echo &#34;== $p ==&#34;

</summary>
```bash
# Install planet assets into public
ASSET_ROOT="apps/app/public/assets/planets"
mkdir -p "$ASSET_ROOT"
rm -rf "$ASSET_ROOT/neptune" "$ASSET_ROOT/mars" "$ASSET_ROOT/moon-2"
unzip -q -o "/Users/liamellis/Downloads/neptune.zip" -d "$ASSET_ROOT/neptune"
unzip -q -o "/Users/liamellis/Downloads/mars (1).zip" -d "$ASSET_ROOT/mars"
unzip -q -o "/Users/liamellis/Downloads/moon.zip" -d "$ASSET_ROOT/moon-2"
# normalize layout
find "$ASSET_ROOT" -type f | head -40
du -sh "$ASSET_ROOT"/*
# check gltf materials quickly
for p in neptune mars moon-2; do
  echo "== $p =="
  rg -n '"name"|baseColor|normal|metallic' "$ASSET_ROOT/$p/scene.gltf" | head -25
done

```

_**Agent (default)**_

I ported the camera choreography from [Makio64/threejs-cinematic-world-zoom](https://github.com/Makio64/threejs-cinematic-world-zoom) — the part that actually makes the zoom cinematic — and dropped a playable Design Lab so you can pick the exact shot before I wire it into production.

## What I built (behind the design-lab, not yet in production)

- **`lib/animations/cinematic-shot.ts`** — pure, framework-free choreography (12/12 unit tests passing via `bun test`). The three load-bearing ideas from the repo:
  - **Geometric (log-space) distance** — `mixLog(d0,d1,t)`. Constant zoom rate = constant rate of change of *log* distance. This is why the current linear rig felt like "stall then slam."
  - **Per-channel easing** — distance / azimuth / pitch / FOV / roll each on their own bezier or monotone-cubic (`smoothTrack`) curve. That offset is what makes it read as a *shot*.
  - **FOV as a real channel** + bank/roll (your rig never animated the lens).
  - Five presets: **Descent · Dive · Orbit · Flyby · Hyperzoom**.
- **`lib/animations/apply-orbit-state.ts`** — resolves a shot onto the camera orbiting the globe (singularity-free eye basis; no DOM scale, ever).
- **Lab:** `/design-lab/home-celestial/cinematic` — real production Earth PBR + starfield, **Play** the autorun timing or **scrub** it like the Act-2 scroll journey, and tune Far/Near/Duration live.

I deliberately did **not** port the Google 3D-tiles / Cesium / sun-solver / recorder — those need API keys and land on real lat/lon coordinates; our hero orbits a globe in space, so the rig collapses to a clean spherical orbit.

## What I need from you before wiring it in

Open **[http://localhost:3007/design-lab/home-celestial/cinematic](http://localhost:3007/design-lab/home-celestial/cinematic)**, try each shot (Play + scrub), then tell me:
